name: Auberge du Jeu de Paume
insider_take: This former royal tennis court turned luxury retreat sits in the shadow of the magnificent Château de Chantilly, where French aristocracy once played the precursor to modern tennis.
whats_special: The hotel occupies a historic 18th-century building that once housed the jeu de paume courts of the Prince de Condé. You're staying where French nobility perfected their game just steps from one of France's most important châteaux, home to the second-largest collection of ancient paintings after the Louvre.
pro_tip: Book the château visit early morning before crowds arrive - you'll have the stunning Galerie des Batailles and priceless manuscripts nearly to yourself, plus the famous Chantilly cream was invented right here in the castle kitchens.
dont_miss: The Living Museum of the Horse in the château's Great Stables - it's housed in what many consider the most beautiful stable building in the world, and the equestrian shows are absolutely spectacular.
pros: Historic château setting with authentic French architecture
Close proximity to Château de Chantilly and horse racing facilities
Elegant rooms with period furnishings and modern amenities
Peaceful countryside location just 30 minutes from Paris
cons: Small boutique property with limited facilities
Requires car or taxi for exploring surrounding area
